questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience asian culture and I had heard a lot of good things about the National University of Singapore (NUS).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We got plenty of emails regarding our stay but other than that there were next to none help to be found upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I didn't get any assistance when I arrived at my study assistance. Unfortunately, I didn't get on campus housing and therefore were a bit excluded from  campus life and it was quite difficult to figure out how things on campus worked. Furthermore, they didn't facilitate an orientation upon arrival. I found this quite disappointing because I was under the impression that NUS was quite good at and had a lot of experience with welcoming exchange students. I think this could have made a huge difference to my university experience.
They did try to implement a buddy system so you were teamed up with a local student but as a lot of the buddies were first year students they were busy to get used to uni life and therefore didn't have much time to meet up and help in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got the final confirmation that I didn't get housing on campus two weeks before I had to leave for Singapore so it was really difficult to find something affordable. Luckily, I ended up finding accommodation with other exchange students from KU in a co-living space which worked out well even though it was very expensive for what it was and especially compared to student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult to get integrated into campus life as a lot of the activities are connected to student housing and are therefore not accessible to students living off campus. Furthermore, the incentive to go to campus the days you don't have classes are very small as it took an hour to go there. However, I ended up really liking living further towards the city center and were able to get more of a feel for the city than I would have done if I lived on campus. So there is definitely both pros and cons with both situations, so fear not if you don't get on campus housing. I still had an amazing semester. I would recommend even though you signed up for student housing to check your options off campus as well so you don't end up in the same situation as me;)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as thoroughly process because you will get a lot of emails throughout but if you just do it step by step it's manageable. NUS is quite technology forward so everything can be done online through their website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn't need any help with the process but I believe they both have a support email and number (which is a bit inconvenient with the time difference plus its expensive).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted in the first round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the emails and 'just' do it step by step.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You can definitely feel that the university is one of the best in the world. In general are the students really hard working and academically strong. Their grading system is a bit different from ours which means only a few can get the best grade, however, I heard it is difficult to fail your courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You had less hours in general than back home but otherwise it was pretty similar. I had both lectures and tutorials but not any laboratory hours since I chose courses without.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Computational Thinking for Scientist, Organic Synthesis: The Disconnection Approach, Instrumental Analysis II

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed computational thinking for scientist which was an introduction to Python. The course was really well put together and I learned a lot, so can definitely recommend that if you are looking to learn some programming.
Organic Synthesis: The Disconnection Approach is also a good but difficult course if you are into organic chemistry.
I found Instrumental Analysis II boring as it is mainly theoretical analytical chemistry.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was way more expensive when you are living off campus compared to living on campus where a meal plan often is included as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are very expensive in Singapore but it is affordable to eat out at hawker centers and on campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They do have a wide variety of activities both for the local students and a few specific events for exchange students. However, they seem way less accessible when living off campus. For example is it not possible to join certain sport activities when living off campus. However I enjoyed water polo once pr week and they had an event in the beginning of the semester where you could check out available activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If possible I would definitely recommend joining a sport.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed traveling around the rest of south east asia and can definitely recommend that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy as Singapore is a great city to live in. It is super easy to get around and everyone is super welcoming and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining a sport or other activities/events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is amazing in Singapore so would recommend being open minded and trying new things even though it might look unusual compared to what you are used to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Look for accommodation in a timely manner (also if you applied for on campus housing)
2) Try all the food
3) Travel!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though I had a lot of fun traveling around South East Asia it was also rewarding to explore Singapore and using the amazing city it is.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring both the city and the rest of South East Asia.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The housing situation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
